P1:
Roblox's Jan 14, 2026 Async rename covered 46 methods. Three of yours are in it:
- Player:LoadCharacter -> Player:LoadCharacterAsync
- BadgeService:AwardBadge -> BadgeService:AwardBadgeAsync
- MarketplaceService:GetProductInfo -> MarketplaceService:GetProductInfoAsync
Instance:WaitForChild and RemoteFunction:InvokeServer were NOT renamed (nor InvokeClient or BindableFunction:Invoke). They keep their current names.
Do the old names still work? Yes. The deprecation is informational only: same behaviour, no removal date. Use the Async names in new code and wrap these yielding calls in pcall. Other renames in the same batch include PlayerOwnsAsset -> PlayerOwnsAssetAsync and TeleportService:ReserveServer -> ReserveServerAsync.
P2:
Turning it on: it is opt-in (full release July 9, 2026). Set Workspace.AuthorityMode = Server (Workspace > Server Authority).
Settings it forces:
- Workspace.StreamingEnabled = Enabled
- NextGenerationReplication = Enabled
- SignalBehavior = Deferred
- UseFixedSimulation = Enabled
- PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem = Enabled
Where predicted logic lives: in a ModuleScript in ReplicatedStorage, required by both server and client and registered with RunService:BindToSimulation(fn). It can re-run during resimulation after a misprediction, so keep it deterministic. Read input from InputActions, not UserInputService. Destroying or reparenting instances inside bound functions errors. Client-only visuals (VFX, sound) go in RenderStepped and must tolerate rollback.
Clock: use time(), the simulation clock. Do not use tick(), os.time(), os.clock() or task.wait() timing.
Gotchas: only the first 64 attributes replicate. A game that was not built for streaming gets "missing parts" bugs when this is turned on.
P3:
Property: Workspace.PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem.
Rollout:
- Phase 1, June 2026: opt-in, default Disabled.
- Phase 2, early 2027 (planned): default becomes Enabled.
- Phase 3, mid 2027 (planned): the property is removed and the legacy UserInputService/ContextActionService-based player scripts are gone.
Server Authority mode already forces the property Enabled.
Code at risk:
- Code that reaches into PlayerModule internals, e.g. require(PlayerModule):GetControls(), ControlModule or Enable/Disable calls, or the camera and control modules.
- Forked or copied PlayerScripts. Keep them with StarterPlayer.CreateDefaultPlayerModule = Disabled, otherwise the engine overrides them.
- Code that relies on the old ContextActionService input sinking or binding priority. Custom menus that should block movement need an InputContext with a higher Priority and Sink = true.
P4:
Change (DevForum, Oct 21, 2026): "platform-integrated chat". Roblox renders all chat itself. You opt in with TextChatService.PlatformIntegratedChat = Enabled (Studio only, not scriptable).
Effects for games:
- TextChatMessage.Text and .Translation return "" (with a warning). No API exposes message content any more.
- OnIncomingMessage and Player.Chatted give no text. PrefixText is unsupported.
- Custom chat UI must use the TextChannelWindow instance, with Target set to a TextChannel, instead of your own rendered message list.
- Commands must be TextChatCommand. SendAsync presets are replaced by Quick Words.
- Keyword triggers, chat minigames and profanity counters break.
- Other player-written text (signs, pet names) must still be filtered and rate-limited to 1 submission per minute per player, or sent through a TextChannel.
Timeline: opt-in testing now through Feb 2027. Default on with opt-out from Feb 2027. Required in May 2027. One announcement line says March for the opt-out stage, so treat May 2027 as the hard deadline.
P5:
Limits are per experience, per minute, and shared with Open Cloud. The base changed from 250 to 300 on 2026-07-29.
- Write budget = 300 + 20 x CCU per minute.
- Read = 300 + 40 x CCU. Remove = 300 + 40 x CCU. List = 300 + 2 x CCU.
UpdateAsync costs 1 read + 1 write against the budgets. Per-server limits still exist and can be lowered with SetRateLimitForRequestType. Check headroom with DataStoreService:GetRequestBudgetForRequestType.
Storage = 500 MB + 1 MB x lifetime players (unique users). It counts the latest version of each key, compressed.
Per-key throughput: 4 MB/min write, 25 MB/min read, each request rounded up to the next KB.
Each request-type queue holds 30 requests; overflow fails with errors 301-306.
Gotcha: Open Cloud jobs such as migrations draw from the same pool and can throttle live servers.
P6:
What you must show players:
- Before purchase, every possible crate outcome with numeric odds that sum to 100%. Long lists can sit behind a clearly labelled Info/Odds button; a bare (i) icon is not enough.
- The rules cover indirect Robux paths. Gems bought with Robux make Gem-priced crates paid random items, and the same goes for keys, tickets and bundles.
- The Luck Potion is an odds-modifying item. Show the resulting numeric odds before it is bought. While it is active, the displayed odds must update, including for server-wide luck bought by someone else.
What you must check for each player:
- Call PolicyService:GetPolicyInfoForPlayerAsync on the server.
- If ArePaidRandomItemsRestricted is true or missing, block paid crates and the Luck Potion for that player. Hide them, or offer a free earnable path or a direct-purchase alternative.
- IsPaidItemTradingAllowed gates trading of paid outcomes.
- Fail closed if the call errors, and retry later.
Enforce the gate in every server purchase, ProcessReceipt and trade handler. Build the displayed odds and the actual roll from the same table.
P7:
What they are: age-based tiers. Roblox Kids is ages 5-8 and Roblox Select is ages 9-15. They only see experiences that passed an extra evaluation; everything else is 16+ only for them.
What the game needs:
- A maturity rating of Minimal or Mild for Kids (Minimal, Mild or Moderate 9+ for Select), with the content questionnaire fully completed.
- To pass the Kids/Select evaluation: engagement from age-checked players plus a safety review.
- Social hangouts, games about sensitive issues and free-form drawing games are excluded by default.
What the creator needs:
- A completed age check (facial estimation if under 18, government ID if 18+).
- 2-Step Verification on.
- Either 2 consecutive months of Roblox Plus/Premium or a refundable publishing fee (the Publish page says 1,000 Robux).
These rules apply to the first release, every update and every audience change. Engagement thresholds differ across Roblox pages, so check the Audience Reach dashboard in Creator Hub.
P8:
Creator Rewards (replaced engagement-based payouts) pays in two ways:
- Daily Engagement: 5 Robux per day for each qualifying Active Spender. That is a user who spent USD 9.99+ in the last 60 days, played your game 10+ minutes, and had it among the first 3 experiences they launched that day.
- Audience Expansion: 35% of a new or reactivated user's first USD 100 of qualifying purchases within 60 days, paid out after a 60-day hold.
Eligibility: a Share Link, 10+ minutes of play, 100+ average DAU, and an ID-verified owner.
DevEx rates:
- Standard: USD 0.0038 per Earned Robux.
- 2026 US 18+ rate: USD 0.0054 per Robux. It applies only to qualifying spend by age-checked US 18+ buyers in R15 experiences: passes, developer products, subscriptions, private servers and Paid Access. Avatar items never qualify.
- Legacy balances from before Sep 5, 2025 exchange first at USD 0.0035.
Cash-out rules: minimum 30,000 Earned Robux, age 13+, one request per month.
G1:
Rules for ProcessReceipt:
1. Set exactly one callback, on the server.
2. Make it idempotent per receiptInfo.PurchaseId. Record processed PurchaseIds in the player's saved data or a DataStore, and if the ID is already there, return PurchaseGranted without granting again.
3. If the player is not in the server (GetPlayerByUserId returns nil), or their data is not loaded, return NotProcessedYet.
4. Grant the item and persist it. Use UpdateAsync with the PurchaseId inside pcall, and return PurchaseGranted only after the save succeeds. On any error return NotProcessedYet, never PurchaseGranted.
5. Never yield forever, and never throw. A callback that errors counts as not processed.
Why players are charged and get nothing: the code returns PurchaseGranted even though the grant or save failed or the player had left, so Roblox considers the purchase done.
Why players get an item twice: Roblox re-sends receipts that were not acknowledged (on rejoin or on another server). Without a PurchaseId check, or when the grant succeeds but the save or return fails, the item is granted again. A non-atomic Get-then-Set race causes the same thing.
G2:
When to use UpdateAsync: whenever the new value depends on the old one (currency, inventory, counters), whenever several servers could write the same key (teleports, rejoins, trading), and for session locking. It is an atomic read-modify-write, and it retries on conflict. SetAsync blindly overwrites, so a stale server can clobber newer data (rollback or dupes). Use SetAsync only for a value that is truly independent of the previous one.
Rules for the transform function:
- It may run several times, so keep it pure and free of side effects. No granting items or firing remotes inside it.
- It must not yield: no waits and no other DataStore calls.
- Return the new value, or return nil to cancel the write.
- Treat the old value as possibly nil (new player) or of an old schema version.
- Do not mutate shared state outside it. Return a serializable value under the 4 MB key limit.
- Check the session lock or version inside it, and cancel by returning nil if another server owns the data.
Cost: 1 read + 1 write against the budgets. Wrap the call in pcall with retry/backoff.
G3:
Not safe.
1. NaN passes. NaN < 0 and NaN > Gold are both false, and typeof(NaN) is "number". Inf is caught by the max check, but non-integer values like 0.5 also pass.
2. No integer check and no upper sanity cap.
3. No rate limit or debounce, so spamming offers works.
4. Time-of-check vs time-of-use. Gold is only checked, not reserved. A player can create several offers totalling more than their balance, or spend the gold before the trade completes, which dupes gold.
5. player.Gold may be missing, or it may be client-visible state.
Fix:
```lua
offerRemote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, gold)
  if typeof(gold) ~= "number" or gold ~= gold or gold % 1 ~= 0 then return end
  if gold <= 0 or gold > 1e9 then return end
  if not rateOk(player) then return end
  local data = Profiles[player]; if not data then return end
  if gold > data.Gold - data.Escrow then return end
  data.Escrow += gold          -- reserve now
  createOffer(player, gold)    -- re-validate & move escrow atomically on accept
end)
```
Keep the authoritative balance in server data, not a client-replicated Value. When the trade completes, re-check and transfer both sides inside one locked, atomic save.
G4:
Why it gets wiped: the Animator writes Motor6D.Transform every step for every joint that a playing track keys. Heartbeat runs after that, but the animation step that follows overwrites it again, so your aim never shows. Writing in PreRender or Heartbeat loses to the Animator.
Where and how: write procedural offsets in RunService.PreSimulation (after animation is applied, before physics and rendering). Compose with the animated value rather than replacing it:
```lua
RunService.PreSimulation:Connect(function()
  motor.Transform = aimCF * motor.Transform  -- aim on top of idle
end)
```
Use aim * Transform (outside the clip) or Transform * aim (inside the clip's space). Don't accumulate Transform = Transform * R on joints the animation doesn't key, because it compounds every frame. You could also take the barrel joint out of the idle animation.
When to edit C0 instead: C0/C1 is the joint's rest offset. The Animator never overwrites it, and it persists and replicates. Use it for a static or rarely changing offset, such as a permanent mount angle or server-authoritative aim that should replicate. Transform is for per-frame, local, animation-layered motion. Note that new R15 rigs may use AnimationConstraint instead of Motor6D.
G5:
Roblox resolves animations per joint, not per whole animation. For each joint, only the tracks that key that joint compete:
1. AnimationPriority decides first. Order: Core < Idle < Movement < Action < Action2 < Action3 < Action4. The highest priority that keys the joint wins.
2. Tracks at the same priority blend by weight.
3. Weights fill from the top down. Start with a remaining weight of 1. If the higher priority's total weight is at least 1, lower priorities get nothing. If it is below 1, the remainder goes to lower priorities.
So Swing (Action, weight 1) plus Walk (Movement) gives a pure swing on the arm. Swing at weight 0.6 lets 40% of the walk show through.
Your bug: the swing was probably authored or left at Core or Movement priority (the same as or lower than the walk), or it plays at a low weight, so the walk dominates or averages it out.
Fix: set the Action priority on the asset or with track.Priority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Action before Play, and play it at weight 1: track:Play(0.1, 1, 1).
Adjust live with track:AdjustWeight(weight, fadeTime). The fade is linear. A weight below 1 with nothing beneath it blends toward the rest pose.
G6:
Why: a unit-scale mismatch. Blender's default unit is metres, and the FBX exporter writes the file in centimetres (unit scale 100), unless "Apply Scalings" is set. Studio's importer reads that as 100x. Blender also defaults to a 1 m = 1 unit scene while Roblox treats 1 unit as 1 stud.
Recommended FBX export settings:
- Apply Scalings: FBX Units Scale, with Scale 1.0, and Apply Unit and Apply Transform as appropriate. Alternatively set scene Unit Scale 0.01 or export at Scale 0.01. Pick one method, not several.
- Forward -Z, Up Y. Selected objects only. Apply modifiers. Add Leaf Bones off. Bake Animation with Simplify 0 for clips.
- Model at 1 Blender unit = 1 stud and compare against a ~5-stud-tall R15 dummy. Apply scale (Ctrl+A) before exporting.
Fix it at export, not by rescaling in Studio. Rescaling a rigged model breaks animation translations. Studio's importer also has a scale/unit option for one-off fixes. Using .glb avoids most of these unit issues.
G7:
Why: the glTF/GLB exporter's "Apply Modifiers" option (Include > Data > Mesh) is off by default. It exports the base mesh only, so the Mirror half and the Bevel geometry don't exist in the file.
Fix: enable Apply Modifiers in the exporter, or apply the modifiers manually (Ctrl+A on each) on a copy before exporting.
The catch: with Apply Modifiers on, shape keys (morph targets / FACS facial data) are not exported, because Blender can't apply modifiers to meshes that have shape keys. The Armature modifier is excluded, so skinning still survives.
So for static or rigid meshes, just turn it on. For meshes with shape keys, apply the Mirror and Bevel by hand first (with a shape-key-preserving workflow or add-on), then export with the option off.
Also mark sharp edges or use Auto Smooth/normals so bevels shade correctly.
G8:
Problem 1, stretching: fromScale(0.3, 0.3) means 30% of width and 30% of height. Screens have different aspect ratios, so the frame's shape changes.
Fix: add a UIAspectRatioConstraint (AspectRatio = 1, AspectType = FitWithinMaxSize, DominantAxis set as needed). Or size one axis with Scale and keep the ratio, or use Offset plus a single UIScale for a 1920x1080 design.
Problem 2, notch and top bar: content placed at (0,0) sits under device cutouts or the Roblox top bar. That happens when the ScreenGui uses ScreenInsets = None or DeviceSafeInsets, or when IgnoreGuiInset is true.
Fix: set ScreenGui.ScreenInsets = Enum.ScreenInsets.CoreUISafeInsets (the default, recommended for interactive UI), which avoids both the notch and the Roblox top bar. Add a small margin. For custom rows inside the top bar, use TopbarSafeInsets and read GuiService.TopbarInset live with GetPropertyChangedSignal; don't hard-code 36/58 px.
Full-screen art goes in a separate ScreenGui with ScreenInsets = None.
T1:
```lua
local RS = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local BuyItem = RS.Remotes.BuyItem
local Catalog = require(game.ServerStorage.ItemCatalog) -- [id] = {Price=..., MaxQty=...}
local Data = require(game.ServerScriptService.PlayerData) -- server-side profiles

local lastBuy = {}
game.Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(p) lastBuy[p] = nil end)

BuyItem.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, itemId, quantity)
  -- rate limit
  local now = os.clock()
  if lastBuy[player] and now - lastBuy[player] < 0.3 then return end
  lastBuy[player] = now
  -- type/value validation
  if typeof(itemId) ~= "string" or #itemId > 50 then return end
  if typeof(quantity) ~= "number" or quantity ~= quantity
     or quantity % 1 ~= 0 or quantity < 1 or quantity > 99 then return end
  local item = Catalog[itemId]          -- server-owned price, never client's
  if not item then return end
  local profile = Data.Get(player)
  if not profile then return end
  local cost = item.Price * quantity
  if profile.Coins < cost then return end
  profile.Coins -= cost                 -- deduct & grant in same step, no yield between
  profile.Items[itemId] = (profile.Items[itemId] or 0) + quantity
  Data.MarkDirty(player)
end)
```
The client sends only intent. The server owns prices and the balance, validates types, NaN, integers and ranges, and rate-limits.
T2:
```lua
-- On join
local ok, data = pcall(store.UpdateAsync, store, key, function(old)
  old = old or newDefault()
  local lock = old.Lock
  if lock and lock.JobId ~= game.JobId and os.time() - lock.Time < 1800 then
    return nil                       -- locked by another server: cancel
  end
  old.Lock = {JobId = game.JobId, Time = os.time()}
  return old
end)
-- if cancelled/failed: retry w/ backoff (~6x, few s apart, teleport saves land), else kick
-- On autosave (every ~60-120s, jittered) UpdateAsync: verify Lock.JobId == game.JobId,
--   write data + refresh Lock.Time; if lock not ours -> stop saving, kick (data stolen)
-- On leave / before teleport: UpdateAsync save data AND clear Lock (Lock = nil)
-- BindToClose: release+save all players in parallel, finish < 30s
-- Purchases/trades: store processed PurchaseIds/trade ids in the same document
```
Why it stops duplication: only the server holding the lock can write. A new server waits until the old server's final save releases the lock, or until it goes stale (dead server), so a stale copy never overwrites newer data. Use UpdateAsync everywhere, never SetAsync. Before teleporting, save and release the lock first, then call TeleportAsync. ProfileStore/ProfileService implement this pattern.

T4:
Diagnosis: FireServer automatically passes the sending Player as the first argument to OnServerEvent. The client also passed LocalPlayer, so on the server `player` is the real sender and `amount` is the extra Player instance. The 50 ends up as the third argument, and Instance + 1 errors.
Fix: never pass the player yourself.
```lua
-- client
remote:FireServer(50)
-- server
remote.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, amount)
  if typeof(amount) ~= "number" or amount ~= amount then return end
  print(amount + 1)
end)
```
Also validate the value on the server, and never trust a player argument sent by the client; always use the implicit first parameter. (FireClient is different: there you pass the target player explicitly.)
T5:
Why: in Studio solo play the local player can join before your server Script runs and connects Players.PlayerAdded, for example because the script waits on something or requires a slow module first. PlayerAdded does not fire for players already in the server, so that player never gets leaderstats. Live servers start before anyone joins, so it rarely shows there.
Standard fix: connect the handler, then loop over the players already present.
```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local function onPlayerAdded(player)
  local ls = Instance.new("Folder")
  ls.Name = "leaderstats"
  local coins = Instance.new("IntValue")
  coins.Name = "Coins"
  coins.Parent = ls
  ls.Parent = player
end
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(onPlayerAdded)
for _, p in Players:GetPlayers() do
  task.spawn(onPlayerAdded, p)
end
```
Also connect before any yields (WaitForChild, DataStore loads) in that script.

local BADGE_ID = 123456

local function awardFinishBadge(player: Player)
  -- optional: skip if already owned (saves a call / avoids noise)
  local okHas, has = pcall(BadgeService.UserHasBadgeAsync, BadgeService, player.UserId, BADGE_ID)

T8:
What is going on: Workspace.MeshStreamingAndImprovedLoDs is Enabled (mesh streaming with cloud-generated LoDs). In that mode the engine picks the level of detail itself by distance and screen size, and MeshPart.RenderFidelity is ignored. Precise has no effect, so the meshes still swap to lower LoDs far away. This appears in published or live games, and it may also appear in Studio once the rollout makes Default mean Enabled.
What to check and fix:
1. Check the Workspace property. If you need the old behaviour, set it to Disabled. The phase 2 rollout (Default maps to Enabled, around July 2026) is not confirmed to have shipped.
2. Otherwise design for it. Keep hero meshes' triangle budget reasonable at the source, and split large meshes so LoD and streaming work per part.
3. RenderFidelity only affects rendering. Collision fidelity is separate and unaffected.
Also make sure the model isn't being streamed out or replaced by a low-detail model through ModelStreamingMode/LevelOfDetail (StreamingMesh) on its parent Model.
